correctness.rationale: The polyhedral weighted isotonic projection has active-cell linear parts equal to positive-mass averaging on connected pooled cover components. In a cyclic Hasse graph these are cyclic arcs. Random representatives and disjoint forward paths prove nonexpansivity for equal variation weights. Each Hasse edge is individually poolable because it is a genuine cover; an explicit local 0-1 direction forces each edge weight to dominate a positive convex mean of its neighbors. The cyclic minimum principle forces uniformity. All quantifiers and the n>=4 boundary are specified. The 59,460 exact tests and 66 rigidity cases supplement rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a complete structural characterization of two-input edge-variation stability for every cycle-shaped Hasse partial order and independent positive regression and variation weights. The robust sufficiency under arbitrary observation masses and rigidity under arbitrarily small anisotropy distinguish this result from Hilbert nonexpansivity and the open-path case. A concrete four-vertex diamond realizes strict amplification at the first possible cycle size; no unsupported downstream application is asserted.
